skill.name: unity-editor
skill.description: Control a running Unity Editor from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through unityctl commands for status checks, play mode, logs, tests, screenshots, and editor debugging.
skill.summary: Control and inspect a Unity Editor session with unityctl commands.
skill.author: DirtybitGames

security_audit.summary: The static shell-execution findings are false positives caused by markdown backticks and fenced command examples. The screen-capture upload finding is also a false positive because the cited line only captures a local screenshot. However, the skill includes a real high-risk capability: arbitrary C# execution inside a running Unity Editor.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary C# execution can change project state or access data through the Unity Editor process.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user review before running unityctl script execute, especially for inline code or scripts generated from prompts.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture may expose private assets, scenes, or proprietary project information.
remediation.suggestion: Document that screenshots should only be captured when the user confirms the Editor view is safe to inspect.

remediation.issue: The skill lists many commands that affect a live Editor session.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to run status checks first and avoid lifecycle or play mode commands without user intent.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Start the bridge daemon: `unityctl bridge start`
2. Launch Unity: `unityctl editor run` or manually open the project in Unity Editor
You can also execute code directly with `-c`:
Scripts must define a class with a `public static object Main()` method. The return value is JSON-se
- Run `unityctl status` to check overall project status before running commands
- Always run `unityctl asset refresh` after modifying C# files before entering play mode
- For script execution, write scripts to `tmp/<scriptname>.cs` and execute with `-f`
Run `unityctl status` first to diagnose issues.
| Bridge not responding | `unityctl bridge stop` then `unityctl bridge start` |
| "Project not found" | Run from project directory or use `--project` flag |

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary C# Execution in Unity Editor
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to execute arbitrary C# through unityctl script execute. This is an intended debugging feature, but it can modify assets, inspect scene state, or perform actions with the Unity Editor process privileges if misused.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly describes executing arbitrary C# via Roslyn and provides file and inline execution examples. The risk is contextual rather than a static shell pattern.

content.user_title: Control Unity Editor from AI Assistants
content.value_statement: Unity developers often need fast feedback from a running Editor while coding. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a command guide for unityctl workflows.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops the unityctl bridge daemon for Editor communication.
Launches or stops the Unity Editor from the command line.
Checks project status, bridge health, and Editor connection state.
Runs asset refresh, edit mode tests, and play mode tests.
Reads Unity logs and can capture local Editor screenshots.
Executes C# snippets or script files inside the running Editor for debugging.
limitations: Requires unityctl and a Unity project with the bridge integration configured.
Commands affect the local Unity Editor and may change project state.
Script execution is powerful and should only run reviewed C# code.
It does not replace Unity licensing, project setup, or package installation.

use_cases.title: Debug gameplay during development
use_cases.description: Inspect logs, enter play mode, and query scene objects while iterating on gameplay code.

use_cases.title: Validate changes before review
use_cases.description: Refresh assets, compile scripts, and run Unity tests before sending a change for code review.

use_cases.title: Automate Editor checks from Claude Code
use_cases.description: Use AI-assisted workflows to run repeatable status, test, log, and screenshot commands.

prompt_templates.title: Check Unity connection
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Unity editor skill to check whether unityctl can reach my running Unity Editor.

prompt_templates.title: Compile after C# edits
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh Unity assets, report any compilation errors, and tell me what to fix next.

prompt_templates.title: Run play mode validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Enter play mode, inspect recent Unity logs, then exit play mode and summarize any errors.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect scene state safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a small reviewed C# script in tmp to count active GameObjects, execute it with unityctl, and summarize the result.

output_examples.input: Check whether Unity is ready for commands.
output_examples.output: Unity is running, the bridge is active, and the Editor connection is available. You can now refresh assets or enter play mode.

output_examples.input: Refresh assets after my script changes.
output_examples.output: Asset refresh completed. Unity reported two compiler errors in the gameplay assembly, so play mode should wait until they are fixed.

output_examples.input: Find the Player object position in the current scene.
output_examples.output: The inspected scene contains a Player object. Its current transform position was returned by the reviewed Unity script.

best_practices: Run status checks before Editor, play mode, or script execution commands.
Refresh assets after C# changes before entering play mode or running tests.
Review any C# script before executing it inside the Unity Editor.
anti_patterns: Do not run arbitrary C# generated from untrusted prompts or files.
Do not enter play mode when Unity reports compilation errors.
Do not capture screenshots if the Editor may display private project data.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It guides AI assistants to use unityctl for a local Unity Editor session.

faq.question: Does it require Unity batch mode?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for controlling a running Editor through unityctl.

faq.question: Can it run Unity tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents edit mode and play mode test commands through unityctl.

faq.question: Can it execute C# code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can execute C# in the Editor, so users should review code before running it.

faq.question: Does it upload screenshots?
faq.answer: No evidence of upload is present. The documented command captures a local Unity screenshot.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
